A Bit About Me

I am Antonio Marino, a Postdoctoral Researcher in Computer Science at the University of Cambridge (Prorok Lab). My research merges multi-robot systems with learning-based control to create intelligent, safe, and collaborative autonomous teams.

I'm always open to discussing research ideas, potential collaborations, or recent developments in AI and robotics. Feel free to connect!

Background & Vision

Building on my doctoral research in hybrid learning-control approaches, my work aims to shift multi-robot systems from passive observation to active physical intervention. Because deploying "black box" models on physical systems introduces risk, I advocate for a hybrid approach: conditioning learned policies with provable control structures. By embedding first-order principles inherently into the design, we can achieve rigorous safety, stability, and sim-to-real transferability.

Core Research Focus

My current work bridges theoretical guarantees and real-world application through the following thrusts:

  • Hybrid Learning & Control: Reconciling classical control techniques (e.g., Lyapunov, Contraction Theory) with deep learning to guarantee safety in neural policies.
  • Functional Heterogeneity: Formulating metrics and dynamic coalition frameworks to understand how diverse agents can optimize complex tasks better than homogeneous swarms.
  • Graph Neural Networks (GNNs): Analyzing GNNs as distributed dynamical systems to ensure Input-to-State Stability (ISS) in multi-agent communication.
  • Environment Co-Design & Manipulation: Enabling robot teams to actively reshape their surroundings and collaboratively manipulate complex, deformable objects in unstructured environments.
